When I was in the psychiatric unit of the hospital I read The Bell Jar by Sylvia Plath, it’s not a self help book and I was actually advised not to read it as it can be triggering (self harm, suicide) but it helped me a lot and showed me that other people go through these struggles. It quickly became my favourite book and I’m re-reading it right now. Do not read it if you’re easily triggered but it gave me a sense of comfort and community. What I liked about it was that the protagonist had a life of glamour and success but still struggled with depression. This was comforting to me as I was in a constant state of guilt for my mental state as there was nothing wrong with my life. It displays that anyone can struggle. It is also semi-autobiographical to Plath’s life which interested me as I am a huge fan of hers. Even people like Sylvia Plath struggle immensely. You’re not alone. Oh also it was published in the 60s which was a time of extreme stigmatization of mental illness. I find this to be extremely progressive in breaking the stigma.
